cf.title: Re-read subscription state after lock in AlterSubscription

input.subject: Re-read subscription state after lock in AlterSubscription

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection touches 0001 and 0002: they fix reproduced bugs, copy the existing AlterPublication() re-read, and have reviewer support. The surviving objections are fixable and concern 0003 and 0004 (demand-1, already-exists-1) and the unlocked OWNER TO path (maintenance-fit-2). The backpatch range for 0001 and 0002 is a committer's decision. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 25 messages were visible.

brief.title: Re-read subscription state after taking the lock in ALTER and DROP SUBSCRIPTION
brief.problem: AlterSubscription() reads the subscription catalog row before it takes AccessExclusiveLock, so a concurrent ALTER or DROP leaves it acting on stale data. Before a5918fddf10 this mostly ended in a "tuple concurrently updated" elog(), but conflict_log_destination = 'table' now creates or drops a table from stale state. A reviewer also showed REFRESH PUBLICATION racing DROP SUBSCRIPTION and leaving orphaned pg_subscription_rel rows.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 and 0002 move GetSubscription() and the password_required check after LockSharedObject() in AlterSubscription() and DropSubscription(), re-read the row by OID, and recheck ownership. 0002 also honors missing_ok and runs the DROP hook only after the re-read. 0003 and 0004 add a retry loop like RangeVarGetRelidExtended() that does name lookup, owner check and locking together, for subscriptions and for the ALTER PUBLICATION tables/schemas branch.
user_visible_surface: Concurrent ALTER or DROP SUBSCRIPTION reports "must be owner", "does not exist" or password_required errors instead of "tuple concurrently updated".
DROP SUBSCRIPTION IF EXISTS no longer fails when the subscription is dropped concurrently.
ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (conflict_log_destination = 'table') no longer fails with "relation already exists" under concurrency.
Object access DROP hook for subscriptions now runs after the lock and existence check.
New isolation tests subscription-owner-locking and publication-owner-locking.
author_claims: The bug exists on all supported branches but became more visible after a5918fddf10.
0001 and 0002 are small and the replaced messages are elog() ones, so the author proposes backpatching them.
0003 and 0004 should go to master only.
Without a re-read, a reused ctid after vacuum could in theory corrupt a tuple; the author calls this extremely rare.
v5 fixes the orphaned pg_subscription_rel rows that Shlok Kyal reported.
brief.thread_state: Dilip Kumar, Hayato Kuroda, Zhijie Hou and Amit Kapila support 0001; Shlok Kyal approved 0001 and reviewed 0002, which v6 fixed. Amit Kapila questions 0003 and 0004 as unneeded machinery for a theoretical OID-reuse risk and doubts backpatching; neither point is settled.
unclear: No reviewer has answered Amit Kapila's objection to the retry loops since the author's reply.
The thread does not say whether the orphaned pg_subscription_rel case needs backpatching, or which branches it affects.
The thread does not say how far back 0001 and 0002 would go, given conflict_log_destination exists only in master.
No reviewer has commented on the v6 post-lock owner recheck or the new isolation tests.
The patch does not say if AlterSubscriptionOwner() should also take the subscription object lock.

prior_attempts.title: Fix alter subscription concurrency errors
prior_attempts.who_objected: Amit Kapila, Alvaro Herrera, Tom Lane
prior_attempts.quote: I think the patch as-submitted is pretty uninteresting, mainly because the design of adding bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers objected that adding lock-and-retry lookup code specific to subscriptions does not scale, since the same problem affects other object types. Alvaro Herrera suggested using get_object_address() instead, and Tom Lane added that this might first require improving its error reporting. The author did not post an updated version for several commitfests. He then said his own test-flakiness problem had been worked around and that he was not motivated to address the issue for all DDL commands, and the entry was withdrawn.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: 0001 and 0002 do a single re-read by OID after the lock, which [P2] did not split out. 0003 and 0004 still add subscription- and publication-specific retry loops, which is what [P2] was criticized for.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
prior_attempts.quote: The race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking risks for.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: [P13] was about GRANT role and DROP ROLE, a different area. Its reason bears on the open backpatch question for 0001 and 0002.

objections.title: Retry loops in 0003 and 0004 answer a race no user has reported
objections.failure_scenario: A user drops and recreates a same-named subscription or publication while another session's ALTER waits on the lock. Once 0001 and 0002 are in, that session gets a clear error, and the user retries. 0003 and 0004 would turn that error into a silent success, at the cost of two new lookup-lock-retry loops that every later change to these DDL paths must keep correct.
objections.argument: The material has no field report of the drop-and-recreate or OID-reuse case. Amit Kapila calls it theoretical (messages #17, #20), and the author agrees OID reuse is theoretical (message #21). The author argues consistency: DROP PUBLICATION already retries through get_object_address(). That argument is about design, not demand. Every bug actually shown in the thread, including the orphaned pg_subscription_rel rows in message #23 and the conflict log table errors in message #1, is fixed by the single re-read in 0001 and 0002.
objections.author_must_show: Which concrete failure, seen by a user or a test, still happens with 0001 and 0002 applied and is fixed only by the retry loops in 0003 and 0004?

critic.reasoning: Message #21 cites 4240e429d0c and b3ad5d02c9c as precedent for retrying on drop-and-recreate, but shows no failure that remains after 0001 and 0002. Amit Kapila's objection in messages #17 and #20 has no reviewer answer.

objections.title: Retry loops in 0003/0004 duplicate get_object_address() instead of reusing it
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch fixes missing_ok handling or error reporting in the get_object_address() retry loop. The private copies in subscriptioncmds.c and publicationcmds.c keep the old behaviour, and nothing fails when they drift apart. Users find out when DROP PUBLICATION and DROP SUBSCRIPTION handle the same concurrent case differently.
objections.argument: Message #21 says get_object_address() already does lookup, lock and retry for OBJECT_SUBSCRIPTION and OBJECT_PUBLICATION, and that DROP PUBLICATION uses it. 0003 and 0004 instead add two more copies of the RangeVarGetRelidExtended() loop for one object class each. An earlier subscription-only retry loop was withdrawn after reviewers called bespoke lock code for subscriptions a design that does not scale, and pointed to get_object_address() [P2]. 0001 and 0002 follow the existing AlterPublication() re-read by OID and are not affected by this objection.
objections.author_must_show: Why can AlterSubscription(), DropSubscription() and the AlterPublication() tables/schemas branch not get their locked OID from get_object_address(), extended if needed?

critic.reasoning: Message #21 confirms get_object_address() already retries for publications and subscriptions, and the thread does not say why 0003 and 0004 cannot use it. [P2] fits: the same subscription-only loop drew the same suggestion.

objections.title: Post-lock owner recheck does not cover ALTER SUBSCRIPTION OWNER TO
objections.failure_scenario: Session 1 runs ALTER SUBSCRIPTION SET and passes the post-lock owner recheck. Session 2 runs ALTER SUBSCRIPTION OWNER TO, which takes no subscription object lock, and commits. Session 1 then acts on an owner that is already stale, and the user still gets "tuple concurrently updated".
objections.argument: The v6-0001 commit message says owner changes "do not yet acquire the subscription object lock". So the new recheck in 0001 and 0002 narrows the window but does not close it. Message #1 used this same fact to argue that a recheck is pointless, and message #25 reverses that without fixing the lock protocol. That leaves one subscription DDL outside the locking rule that every later DDL must follow, and a reviewer can easily miss this.
objections.author_must_show: Should AlterSubscriptionOwner() take AccessExclusiveLock on the subscription object in this series, so that the post-lock owner recheck becomes a real guarantee?

critic.reasoning: The v6-0001 commit message says owner changes "do not yet acquire the subscription object lock", so the recheck leaves a window. The gap exists before the patch, but v6 reverses message #1 without saying whether AlterSubscriptionOwner() should take the lock.

refuted.title: Retry loops in 0003 and 0004 repeat a design rejected earlier
refuted.failure_scenario: After 0003 and 0004, subscriptions and the ALTER PUBLICATION tables/schemas branch each carry their own lookup, owner check and lock loop. Other ALTER paths for these and other object types keep the old pattern. A later change to the lookup or locking rules has to be applied by hand in each copy, and a missed copy fails silently.
refuted.argument: [P2] re-fetched the subscription after the lock with a retry loop and was withdrawn on the objection that bespoke subscription lock code does not scale. A reviewer there pointed to get_object_address() instead. Message #21 notes that DROP PUBLICATION already gets this retry through get_object_address(), but 0003 adds a separate loop for DROP SUBSCRIPTION and 0004 a third copy. The thread does not say why these paths cannot use get_object_address() or a shared helper, and message #17 and message #20 question the loops on other grounds.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can DROP and ALTER SUBSCRIPTION and the ALTER PUBLICATION branch not use get_object_address() or one shared helper instead of separate retry loops?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which makes the same get_object_address() point and also states that 0001 and 0002 are not affected.

refuted.title: Subscription-only retry loop duplicates get_object_address() for one object type
refuted.failure_scenario: After 0003 and 0004, DROP PUBLICATION resolves names through get_object_address(), but DROP SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER of both objects use new copies of the retry loop. A later fix to the lookup, lock and retry logic in get_object_address() then reaches only some of these commands. Concurrent DDL on publications and subscriptions behaves differently, and nobody notices until a race report arrives.
refuted.argument: Message #21 notes that get_object_address() already handles OBJECT_SUBSCRIPTION and OBJECT_PUBLICATION with a retry loop, and that DROP PUBLICATION uses it. 0003 and 0004 still add a hand-written loop modeled on RangeVarGetRelidExtended() and do not say why the existing helper cannot be used. The withdrawn attempt [P2] stalled on the same point: bespoke subscription lock code does not scale, and reviewers there suggested get_object_address(). This concern covers only 0003 and 0004.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can AlterSubscription(), DropSubscription() and the AlterPublication() tables/schemas branch not call get_object_address() instead of carrying their own retry loops?

refuted.title: Owner recheck after lock does not pin ownership while OWNER TO skips the lock
refuted.failure_scenario: A superuser runs ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... OWNER TO newrole just after the old owner's ALTER SUBSCRIPTION passes the post-lock owner recheck. The old owner's command keeps running with authority it no longer has. It stops only if a later CatalogTupleUpdate() fails, and any step done before that runs as the old owner.
refuted.argument: The v6 commit message says owner changes "do not yet acquire the subscription object lock", and message #1 says AlterSubscriptionOwner() takes only RowExclusiveLock on pg_subscription. So the recheck narrows the window and does not close it. The real guarantee is still the "tuple concurrently updated" error, which the patch presents as a confusing message to remove. Backpatching an owner recheck that reads as a privilege guarantee, while OWNER TO stays unlocked, leaves the actual rule undocumented on every branch.
refuted.author_must_show: Should AlterSubscriptionOwner() take AccessExclusiveLock on the subscription object, and if not, which step after the owner recheck can act on the publisher before CatalogTupleUpdate() fails?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. This version also names no step that acts with the old owner's authority, and the unlocked OWNER TO path exists before the patch.

refuted.title: Hand-written retry loops per object type in 0003 and 0004
refuted.failure_scenario: 0003 and 0004 add two more copies of the RangeVarGetRelidExtended() pattern, one in subscriptioncmds.c and one in publicationcmds.c. A later patch changes the shared lookup-and-lock rules or the ownership check in get_object_address(). The copies are not updated, and nothing fails until a new race shows up in the field.
refuted.argument: [P2] stopped an earlier subscription patch with this kind of loop because "bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale" and pointed to get_object_address(). Message #21 says DROP PUBLICATION already gets a retry loop through get_object_address(), so a shared path exists. Amit Kapila (message #17, message #20) calls the OID-reuse risk theoretical and suggests a code comment, and no reviewer has answered since message #21. The prose does not say why ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER PUBLICATION cannot use the existing path.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION and ALTER PUBLICATION not resolve and lock through get_object_address() instead of carrying their own retry loops?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila takes part in the thread, supports 0001 and questions 0003, 0004 and the backpatch. The owner must know subscription DDL locking.
committability.liability: For 0001 and 0002: changed error paths and hook timing in ALTER and DROP SUBSCRIPTION, on every branch that gets the backpatch. For 0003 and 0004: two retry loops that later changes to lookup and locking rules must keep in step.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted six versions and fixed the orphaned pg_subscription_rel case a reviewer reported, which suggests he stays for fixes.

priority.reason: 0001 and 0002 are small, fix reproduced races in concurrent subscription DDL and have reviewer support, so they can proceed alone. 0003 and 0004 raise the burden and can wait until the get_object_address() and demand questions have answers.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm that every use of subscription state in AlterSubscription() and DropSubscription() now follows the re-read. The interaction of the retry loops with lock release on a changed OID is also unchecked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel tests publication and subscription might fail due to concurrent tuple update
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the publication and subscription regression tests out of a shared parallel group so they run one after the other. Both tests run GRANT/REVOKE on the same pg_database row, which can fail with "tuple concurrently updated".
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found one such failure in a year of buildfarm logs, on v16 and not on master, which is below the project's noise threshold. Running the two tests serially gives up parallelism for that small gain. The serial schedule would likely stay even if someone later fixes the GRANT/REVOKE race. The entry was closed, to be reopened if the failure comes back.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It would be kind of sad to lose all parallelism for these two
tests, and one-failure-per-year is surely below our noise threshold.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix alter subscription concurrency errors
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Amit Kapila, Alvaro Herrera, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixed "tuple concurrently updated" errors from concurrent ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION statements on the same subscription by re-fetching the subscription tuple after acquiring its lock, using a retry loop modeled on dbcommands.c. A later version also allowed ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... OWNER TO to run concurrently with the other subscription commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that adding lock-and-retry lookup code specific to subscriptions does not scale, since the same problem affects other object types. Alvaro Herrera suggested using get_object_address() instead, and Tom Lane added that this might first require improving its error reporting. The author did not post an updated version for several commitfests. He then said his own test-flakiness problem had been worked around and that he was not motivated to address the issue for all DDL commands, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the patch as-submitted is pretty uninteresting, mainly because the
design of adding bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow reads to proceed during FK/trigger drops by reducing relation-level lock from AccessExclusive to ShareRowExclusive
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lowers the relation-level lock taken while dropping foreign key constraints and their RI triggers from AccessExclusiveLock to ShareRowExclusiveLock, so that SELECTs on the other table keep running. A revised patch narrowed the change to RI action triggers on the referenced table and kept AccessExclusiveLock elsewhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the change is unsafe for FK removal, because the planner may have built query plans that rely on the constraint holding, as the comment in AlterTableGetLockLevel explains. He also noted that the first patch lowered the lock for other constraint types, and that dropping a unique constraint can also break existing plans. The author posted a narrower patch, but no one replied to it, and the visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding a foreign key can (and I think does) take a lesser lock,
because the additional constraint won't invalidate any proofs the
optimizer may have made beforehand.  But dropping one seems
problematic.

precedents_retrieved.title: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY support for partitioned indexes. It changes index_drop() to expand a partitioned index into the list of its partition indexes and run the concurrent drop steps on all of them in two transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier disliked the new code path for deleting dependent objects in the partition tree and said the problem needed more design work first. The patch then stopped applying to HEAD, and the author withdrew it until the related patch for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned tables makes progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking
quicky at the patch, I am not much a fan of the new code path
introduced for the deletion of dependent objects in the partition
tree, so my gut is telling me that we need to think harder about the
problem at hand first.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

Diagnosys-by: Andrey Borodin <x4mmm@yandex-team.ru>
Diagnosys-by: Michael Paquier <michael@paquier.xyz>
Diagnosys-by: Andres Freund <andres@anarazel.de>

precedents_retrieved.title: add subscription TAP test option "vcregress subscriptioncheck" for MSVC builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a "subscriptioncheck" option to vcregress.pl so that MSVC builds can run the subscription TAP tests with one command, like "recoverycheck". Later the thread moved to a documentation patch that describes "vcregress taptest" for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan objected to adding more special targets to vcregress.pl, because the generic taptest option already runs any TAP test set with "vcregress taptest src/test/subscription". The author agreed and switched to a documentation patch. Juan José Santamaría Flecha reviewed that patch and asked for a typo fix and new wording, and the visible messages show no revised version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would actually prefer to reduce the number of special things in
vcregress.pl rather than add more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Subscription code improvements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Petr Jelinek posted a set of logical replication subscription patches: cleaner worker exit messages, a split of SetSubscriptionRelState into separate add and update functions, transactional stopping of workers in ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION, syscache access to pg_subscription without a database connection, and finer-grained subscription locking. Masahiko Sawada later took over the remaining patches for the PG11 cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Part of the set was committed: the transactional worker stop in August 2017, and the message and SetSubscriptionRelState patches in April 2018. The remaining patches, the syscache change and the finer-grained locking, were not committed. Peter Eisentraut found that the locking patch no longer applied and that the syscache patch was of little use without it, and he did not want to review that much code so late. Earlier he had asked what the patches fixed, and the entry had waited on the author since the November commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: 0004 doesn't apply anymore, 0003 doesn't seem to be very useful without 0004, as I understand it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert 019_replslot_limit.pl related debugging aids.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert 019_replslot_limit.pl related debugging aids.
Reverted commit(s): Don't fail for > 1 walsenders in 019_replslot_limit, add debug messages.; Add retries for further investigation of 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.; Add further debug info to help debug 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.; Add temporary debug info to help debug 019_replslot_limit.pl failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts most of 91c0570a791, f28bf667f60, fe0972ee5e6, afdeff10526. The
only thing left is the retry loop in 019_replslot_limit.pl that avoids
spurious failures by retrying a couple times.

We haven't seen any hard evidence that this is caused by anything but slow
process shutdown. We did not find any cases where walsenders did not vanish
after waiting for longer. Therefore there's no reason for this debugging code
to remain.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce lock level for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CHECK
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lowers the lock level for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CHECK to ShareRowExclusiveLock, matching what was already done for foreign key constraints. The author argued this is safe because check constraints do not affect running SELECTs until validated; a second patch extended lock reductions to other ALTER TABLE forms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that ADD CHECK updates both pg_class.relchecks and pg_constraint, so with the lower lock a concurrent session can read a relchecks count that does not match pg_constraint and fail in CheckConstraintFetch. He demonstrated this with a debugger. Replacing relchecks with a boolean could fix it, but he doubted the gain was worth the compatibility cost, and the author agreed to return the patch.
matched_queries: alter publication ownership check lock race
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch makes it possible for onlookers to
see a value of pg_class.relchecks that is inconsistent with what
they find in pg_constraint, and then they will blow up.

precedents_retrieved.title: orphaned function
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes QualifiedNameGetCreationNamespace() take a lock on the target schema, so a concurrent DROP SCHEMA cannot leave a function without a namespace. A reviewer added a separate patch that also locks the function's argument types, return type and language.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the schema lock alone does not close the race and needs retry logic like RangeVarGetAndCheckCreationNamespace. He also asked why only this dependency should be covered, and pointed to a general approach based on pg_depend. The author agreed and proposed a different design that checks a catalog snapshot during DROP, but sent no patch. David Steele marked the entry Returned with Feedback because a new patch was needed and, after Alvaro Herrera's comment, the change looked like a new safety feature that could not be back-patched as a bug fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think that actually succeeds in preventing the race, it'll just delay your process till the deletion is committed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
Reverted commit(s): Allow page lock to conflict among parallel group members.; Add assert to ensure that page locks don't participate in deadlock cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the work done by commits 3ba59ccc89 and 72e78d831a.
Those commits were incorrect in asserting that we never acquire any other
heavy-weight lock after acquring page lock other than relation extension
lock. We can acquire a lock on catalogs while doing catalog look up after
acquring page lock.

This won't impact any existing feature but we need to think some other way
to achieve this before parallelizing other write operations or even
improving the parallelism in vacuum (like allowing multiple workers
for an index).

Reverted commit(s): Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 81069a9efc5a374dd39874a161f456f0fb3afba4.

Buildfarm results suggest that some platforms have versions of pselect(2)
that are not merely non-atomic, but flat out non-functional.  Revert the
use-pselect patch to confirm this diagnosis (and exclude the no-SA_RESTART
patch as the source of trouble).  If it's so, we should probably look into
blacklisting specific platforms that have broken pselect.

roaster_notes.note: 0001 and 0002 differ from [P2] by doing a plain re-read by OID after the lock, and the precedents raise no objection against them.

From the compatibility angle, 0001 and 0002 only replace elog() errors with proper ereport() errors and make DROP SUBSCRIPTION IF EXISTS honor missing_ok. They add no syntax, GUC or dump change, and existing scripts do not regress.

The patches change only lock ordering and the timing of catalog reads, so they add no on-disk format, WAL record, wire protocol, catalog column or exported ABI. One open point remains: orphaned pg_subscription_rel rows already created by the REFRESH PUBLICATION and DROP race in message #23 stay in existing clusters, and the proposal does not say whether release notes or a cleanup query should cover them.
There is one objection. The patch otherwise tightens the privilege checks, and the new password_required and owner rechecks do not give non-superusers anything they could not do before.
0001 and 0002 move existing reads after the lock and add no hot-path cost. Only the scope of 0003 and 0004 and the incomplete lock protocol raise maintenance concerns.
0001 and 0002 copy the existing AlterPublication() pattern and fix a real bug; no existing feature or extension already does this, so nothing is raised against them from this angle.
0001 and 0002 fix reproduced bugs and have broad reviewer support, so demand for them is shown. The objection covers only 0003 and 0004.
